robots.action: allowed — /waterdata/ is not among the * disallows (which are /cgi-bin/, /hydro/, /clim_data/rrp/, /info/, /meta/ …); /water/ is explicitly Allow
robots.claude: allowed — robots.txt names no AI crawler at all (12 UAs, none of them ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai)

cors: none — fetch from https://notice.place threw; opaque no-cors reachable in 141 ms. Server-side only, which is where it belongs
licence: "Unless otherwise noted, all material on this page is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution Australia Licence" — https://www.bom.gov.au/waterdata/ (page footer). Note it says "Australia Licence" (3.0 AU), not 4.0; /water/copyright.shtml is 404
validated: the SOS GetObservation on the same station (next entry) returns 0.416 m at 00:00 and 0.415 m at 09:00 on 3 Sep 2026 — same value from the OGC front door and the KiWIS REST front door; and the reading is falling slowly on a dry morning (Open-Meteo rain_48h 1.1 mm at Jan Juc), which is the right direction. NOT validated against an independent gauge owner — WMIS (below) never answered
cadence: AsStored updates every 15 min at Cumberland; BOM's copy of the Barwon and Gellibrand gauges lags 2–3 weeks (coverage ends 17 Aug 2026 on 4 Sep) — read hourly, and print the timestamp, because staleness differs per gauge
verdict: BUILD IT — for Cumberland @ Lorne today, and for Barwon @ Forrest / Gellibrand only once their lag is understood; the waterfall signal is the Cumberland/Erskine catchment and the live gauge is 5 km from Erskine Falls' catchment. Attribution owed.

name: BOM Water Data Online — OGC SOS 2.0 GetObservation
answers: the same series as WaterML 2.0 XML — hourly-mean water course level per station
where: station 235216 CUMBERLAND @ LORNE; any station_no from getStationList works in featureOfInterest
request: curl -sS -A 'whattodo-janjuc/1.0 (+https://www.notice.place)' 'https://www.bom.gov.au/waterdata/services?service=SOS&version=2.0&request=GetObservation&featureOfInterest=http://bom.gov.au/waterdata/services/stations/235216&observedProperty=http://bom.gov.au/waterdata/services/parameters/Water%20Course%20Level&procedure=Pat3_C_B_1_HourlyMean&temporalFilter=om:phenomenonTime,2026-09-03T00:00:00%2b10:00/2026-09-03T23:00:00%2b10:00'   # procedure names come from request=GetDataAvailability&featureOfInterest=…/stations/235216 (35 KB XML; Pat3_* are level, Pat4_* discharge). A guessed procedure returns a 615-byte empty response, not an error
sample: <sos:GetObservationResponse  xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.opengis.net/sos/2.0 http://schemas.opengis.net/sos/2.0/sos.xsd http://www.opengis.net/waterml/2.0 http://schemas.opengis.net/waterml/2.0/wat … <wml2:time>2026-09-03T00:00:00.000+10:00</wml2:time><wml2:value>0.416</wml2:value> … 09:00 → 0.415 (10 points)
licence: as above — CC Attribution Australia, https://www.bom.gov.au/waterdata/
validated: agrees with the KiWIS JSON for the same hour (0.417 AsStored at 10:00 vs 0.415 hourly mean at 09:00)
verdict: Works, but the KiWIS JSON above is the same data in 302 bytes instead of 4 KB of XML — use JSON; keep this as the standards-based fallback.

name: EMV developer feed — Fire Danger Ratings & Total Fire Bans (getFDRTFBJSON / XML)

request: curl -sS -A 'whattodo-janjuc/1.0 (+https://www.notice.place)' -D - 'https://data.emergency.vic.gov.au/Show?pageId=getFDRTFBJSON' | xxd | head   # the XML twin is pageId=getFDRTFBXML
sample: empty body — a single 0x0a byte (Content-Type says application/json; the XML variant is likewise one byte with Content-Type application/xml)
cors: none (fetch from notice.place threw; opaque reachable)
licence: EMV "Emergency data" notice, https://www.emv.vic.gov.au/responsibilities/victorias-warning-system/emergency-data: "The State of Victoria owns any copyright in the data accessed by you from any data feed, site or other source to which this notice applies. The data is provided under a Creative Common Attribution 3.0 Australia licence" and "1. You must identify the source of the data as State of Victoria, Australia. 2. You must include a link to this notice. 3. If you are accessing and publishing emergency warning data, you must display the last date and time an update was received by you from the data feed." — AND the VicEmergency support article (https://support.emergency.vic.gov.au/hc/en-gb/articles/235717508) says "The VicEmergency data feed is not currently available publicly" and to "submit a request". CFA's own RSS page says "Access to Victorian emergency data by third party developers is managed by Emergency Management Victoria" and lists exactly these four getIncident*/getFDRTFB* URLs
validated: the CFA Central RSS (next entry) for the same moment says 'Central: NO RATING' and 'not currently a day of Total Fire Ban' — so an empty developer feed is consistent with 'no rating declared', not with a broken endpoint. Still unvalidated in season: nobody has seen a populated body
cadence: in season, per district, changes daily (~4pm declarations); read hourly
verdict: NEEDS A LICENCE ANSWER, then a November read. The CC BY 3.0 AU notice exists and its three attribution conditions are cheap; what is missing is confirmation that this host is a feed 'to which this notice applies' — the support article says the feed is not public, the CFA page says it is. Email drafted in the worklog. Do not build a parser until the body has data in it.
